subject: Defining 'Done' — success criteria & sprint acceptance plan for Wellness Bridge evaluation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@wellnessbridge.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: success checklist + sprint acceptance for the MAP

Hi Elena —

Great to meet earlier this week. Per our conversation, attached is a compact proposal for what ‘done’ looks like for the 3-week evaluation: a short list of high-confidence success criteria, the exit gates we must clear to move to pilot, and the acceptance tests we’ll run. I wanted to put a simple, prioritized plan on your desk so your engineering and security teams can scan and confirm quickly.

Key asks up front: can you confirm the internal owners for integration (API), security/compliance, and clinical/content validation so we can assign tasks in the MAP worksheet? Also, what’s the preferred blackout window (if any) for your test environment?

High-level success criteria (draft) — short, measurable, and outcome-focused:
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 350ms for 512-token prompt (measured at our regional gateway)
- Throughput: steady-state 40 RPS (sustained for 10 minutes) on your test dataset
- Quality: >=92% intent precision on a 150-prompt evaluation set you provide; hallucination rate <5% on critical clinical prompts
- Safety: content redaction and PI masking pass the redaction smoke test with 0 accepted leaks in 500 requests
- Reliability: failover to fallback model completes within 5s with no data loss in simulated region outage

Exit gates (must-pass before pilot):
1) Security & legal: completed questionnaire + signed DPA
2) Performance: acceptance tests above pass in your network conditions
3) Integration: end-to-end flow (inbound data -> inference -> sanitized output) validated by your API owner
4) Business: mutual approval from product and clinical leads

Acceptance tests (examples we’ll run together):
- Smoke harness: 50 request burst, validate latency & correctness on golden prompts
- Stress run: 30-minute window at 45 RPS to observe cache/batching behavior
- Regression check: run our 150-prompt suite and compare to baseline F1/precision thresholds
- Security check: single-tenant redaction test and KMS key rotation verification

I’ve attached WB-MAP-v1.xlsx — compact tracker with owners, dates, and pass/fail fields. If this looks broadly right I’ll turn this into the MAP in HubSpot and schedule a short alignment call.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Sean — this is helpful and very clear. A few notes from our side:

- Owners: API — Amit Rao (cc'd), Security/Compliance — Priya Kumar (not on this thread yet), Clinical validation — Dr. Elena Soto (me).
- Test window: we prefer early-morning runs (06:00–09:00 PT) to avoid production impact; full stress runs can be scheduled overnight if needed.
- Dataset: we can provide a 150-prompt evaluation pack by EOD Wednesday. It will include 40 high-priority clinical prompts, 60 routing/intent prompts, and 50 edge-case conversation turns.

A few acceptance questions:
1) For the latency P95 target, are you measuring at the public API endpoint or at our VPC/NAT egress? We need numbers that reflect our network.
2) For hallucination measurement, what tooling/heuristic will Redwood use? We need a reproducible method to approve the result.

If you can update the MAP worksheet to include the owners above and a proposed run schedule for 9/3–9/9, we’ll review internally and confirm.

—Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Product, Wellness Bridge

Adding a quick tech validation perspective and a proposed minimal acceptance checklist we’ll run from Redwood side. Sean — feel free to drop these into the spreadsheet as a separate tab (Perf + QA scripts).

Minimal acceptance checklist (technical):
- Network measurement: collect synthetic P95 at both public endpoint and from your VPC egress; acceptance requires both P95 <= 350ms or documentation of delta with remediation plan
- Token accounting: end-to-end token counts verified for 512-token prompts, sample of 50 requests — difference from expected tokenization < 3%
- Model parity: baseline vs candidate model compare — no more than 4% drop in intent precision across the 150-prompt set
- Fallback behavior: simulate instance termination and validate that request routing to fallback returns success (200) and no duplicate-response artifacts
- Observability: traces and token-level cost logs available to your SRE during runs (obligation: 7 days retention for the trial)

On tooling/metrics for hallucination that Elena asked about: we will run both rule-based checks (entity hallucination scoring) and manual spot checks on the 40 clinical prompts. We’ll publish the scoring rubric (see perf-eval-scenarios.md attachment) and record the exact prompts and responses for audit. If needed, we can deliver the rubric as code (small script) so you can reproduce locally.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks all. Quick alignment summary (finalize if correct):

1) Owners and schedule
- API owner (integration): Amit Rao (Wellness Bridge)
- Clinical sign-off: Elena Soto (WB)
- Security/compliance reviewer: Priya Kumar (WB) — Sean to add once Priya joins
- Redwood leads: Sean (program owner), Ben (technical acceptance)
- Proposed runs: 09/04 (smoke harness, morning), 09/05 (stress run, overnight), 09/08 (regression + manual clinical checks)

2) Final success metrics (agreed to test against your network conditions)
- P95 latency <= 350ms at VPC egress (measurement script attached)
- Throughput: maintain >=40 RPS for 10 minutes during stress window
- Intent precision >=92% on the 150-prompt pack; clinical-critical prompts must be >=95% precision
- Hallucination: rule-based score + manual audit; accept if <=5% critical hallucinations
- Redaction: zero PI leaks in 500 requests during redaction smoke test

3) Exit gates to pilot
- Completed security questionnaire + signed DPA
- All technical acceptance checks marked PASS by Ben (or documented mitigations with timeline)
- Clinical signoff by Elena
- Business approval (legal + procurement) — procurement to confirm SOW by 09/12

4) Deliverables from Redwood by 09/03
- Finalized MAP tracker (WB-MAP-v1.xlsx) with tasks/owners/dates
- perf-eval-scenarios.md with scoring rubric and runner commands
- HubSpot MAP created (HS-98765) with milestones

If that list matches your expectations I’ll lock dates in Calendly and send the MAP to HubSpot. Once Priya is added we’ll run the security questionnaire in parallel to technical runs.

Best,
Sean
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
